title: Corporate taxable income — Maple Manufacturing
instructions: Maple Manufacturing, Inc., a calendar-year C corporation, reports 2025 book net income of **$420,000**. Use the data below to compute taxable income and tax.

exhibits.title: Items included in book net income
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Federal income tax expense | 90,000 |
| Interest on municipal bonds | 12,000 |
| Dividends from a 25%-owned domestic corporation | 60,000 |
| Net capital loss (sale of investments) | 15,000 |
| Fines paid to a state agency | 5,000 |
| Business meals | 8,000 |
| Cash charitable contributions | 50,000 |
| Book depreciation | 40,000 |

exhibits.title: Other information
exhibits.content:
- Tax depreciation (MACRS) is **$70,000**.
- Maple has a **$100,000** NOL carryforward from 2021.
- Maple had no capital gains in any year.

rows.label: Taxable income before the charitable deduction, DRD, and NOL
Charitable contribution deduction
rows.explanation: The 10% limit is figured before the charitable deduction, the DRD, and any NOL *carryback*, but after the NOL *carryforward* (IRC §170(b)(2)(D)): 10% × (542,000 − 100,000) = **44,200**. The other 5,800 carries forward 5 years.

rows.label: The $15,000 net capital loss
options: Carried back 3 years and forward 5 years
rows.answer: Carried back 3 years and forward 5 years
rows.explanation: Corporations can't deduct net capital losses currently.

rows.label: The $30,000 depreciation difference
rows.explanation: It reverses over the asset's life.
